source ends ‘tam arborem quam herbam’; translation stops at ‘both the tree and the...’

reason: Long Latin/Greek commentary on arbutus rendered closely; drops one Greek scholion quote, blurs the Apuleius Greek/Roman naming, cuts the final word ‘herbam’.

Source is already English (Loeb list); reproduced verbatim, nothing wrong.

defects.detail: source is alchemical fermentation and ‘Chapitre XXXII. L’imbibition de la Pierre’; translation is a music-theory preface on harmonic proportions 3, 1, 1/3

reason: Translation is of a different text (music theory preface) than the alchemical French source.

defects.detail: ‘vt ex quibus statim pendeat’ (as it depends directly on them) rendered ‘so that it may be known upon what these things immediately depend’
source breaks off ‘quanquam opus de facultatibus naturalibus hoc’; translation completes it as ‘can precede this’

reason: Galenic reading-order passage rendered accurately; one clause misconstrued and the mid-sentence ending completed with invented ‘can precede this’.

defects.detail: footnote ‘¹) τῆς μεταβολῆς libri’ (the MSS read τῆς μεταβολῆς) rendered ‘Books of On Change.’

reason: Preface, Greek book list and notes rendered faithfully; footnote 1 apparatus misread and Strabo page number changed from 15 to 14.

‘REGIVS Troi, regis Phrygiae, filius’ (son of Tros, king of Phrygia) rendered ‘of Troy, the son of the king of Phrygia’

reason: Servius lemmata 250-263 rendered faithfully, but the full critical apparatus is dropped and Tros becomes Troy.
Juvenal Sat. 12 verses rendered line by line faithfully; ‘Arboribus rutulis’ taken as reddened rather than Rutulian.

defects.detail: source breaks off ‘Potius incumbite vt Christo’; translation completes ‘strive to bring the bride to Christ’

reason: Four conditions of the bridegroom’s friend rendered accurately; only the page-final fragment is completed with invented ‘bring the bride’.
Projection passage and Chapter XXXV opening rendered faithfully throughout; nothing wrong found.

defects.detail: ‘etenim eam veluti sopitam odorata exuscitant’ (odorous things rouse venery as if asleep) rendered ‘for it excites the womb as if it were dormant’

reason: Polyp chapter rendered accurately; one clause shifts subject/object (eam = venerem rendered as the womb, odorata as it).
Cicero De officiis III (Regulus, Cyrenaics, Epicurus, Metrodorus) rendered faithfully; nothing wrong found.

defects.detail: ‘quicquid ... vspiam stupet coacta natura’ (whatever nature, compelled, stands aghast at) rendered ‘nature, stunted, has brought together’

reason: Catalogue of court vices and beasts rendered completely and accurately; one clause about nature misconstrued.

‘testaceo paries vestiatur et vestitura calcetur’ rendered ‘covered with fired bricks ... tamped’ (testaceum = potsherd mortar; calcetur = plastered with lime)

reason: Vitruvian excerpts XXIII-XXVI rendered faithfully, but the full critical apparatus is dropped; minor terminology slip on testaceo/calcetur.

defects.detail: source footnotes ‘¹ Frag. 163 (Nauck). ² Frag. 158, 2 (Nauck).’; translation has only ‘¹ Frag. 158, 2 (Nauck).’, dropping Frag. 163 and attaching 158 to note 1
